notes.summary: Physics gives 1–2 questions, mostly NCERT class 6–10 level: SI units, Newton's laws, light (lenses, reflection, scattering), sound and electricity. Learn the 'why' behind daily-life examples.

concepts.title: SI units
concepts.body:
QuantitySI unit
Forcenewton (N)
Work / energyjoule (J)
Powerwatt (W)
Pressurepascal (Pa)
Frequencyhertz (Hz)
Electric currentampere (A)
Chargecoulomb (C)
Resistanceohm (Ω)
Temperaturekelvin (K)
Luminous intensitycandela (cd)
1 horsepower ≈ 746 W. A light year is a unit of distance, not time.

concepts.title: Motion and Newton's laws
concepts.body:
• First law (law of inertia): a body stays at rest or in uniform motion unless a force acts. Example: passengers lurch forward when a bus brakes suddenly.
  • Second law: F = m × a.
  • Third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Example: a rocket moves up as gases rush down; recoil of a gun.
  • Acceleration due to gravity on Earth, g ≈ 9.8 m/s².

concepts.title: Light
concepts.body:
• Convex lens converges light; corrects hypermetropia (long-sightedness). Concave lens diverges light; corrects myopia (short-sightedness).
  • Total internal reflection: used in optical fibres; explains the sparkle of diamonds and mirages.
  • Scattering: the sky looks blue because air scatters blue light more than red. Danger signals are red because red scatters least.
  • Dispersion: a prism splits white light into seven colours (VIBGYOR); a rainbow forms the same way in raindrops.

concepts.title: Sound and electricity
concepts.body:
• Sound needs a medium; it cannot travel in a vacuum. It travels fastest in solids, then liquids, then gases.
  • Human hearing: 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. Below 20 Hz = infrasound; above 20 kHz = ultrasound (used by bats, SONAR).
  • Ohm's law: V = I × R.
  • Household appliances are connected in parallel so each gets the full voltage. A fuse works on the heating effect of current.

varieties.name: Light and optics
varieties.how: Identify the phenomenon (reflection, refraction, TIR, scattering, dispersion), then the example or lens.

example.q: Which lens is used to correct myopia?
steps: Myopia: image forms in front of the retina
A diverging (concave) lens pushes it back onto the retina

varieties.name: Laws and everyday physics
varieties.how: Match the daily-life example to the law or property it shows.

example.q: A rocket works on which law?

tips: Myopia = Minus lens (concave, negative power); Hypermetropia = Plus lens (convex, positive power).
Blue sky = scattering; rainbow = dispersion + reflection + refraction.
Sound speed order: solid > liquid > gas > vacuum (zero).
traps: Light year measures distance, not time.
Sound cannot travel in vacuum, but light can.
Kilowatt-hour (kWh) is a unit of energy, not power.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.solution:
Force is measured in newton (N). 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².
Memory hook: Newton gave the laws of force, so force carries his name.

questions.q: The sky appears blue because of:
questions.solution:
Air molecules scatter shorter wavelengths (blue) much more than longer ones (red), so the sky looks blue.
Memory hook: 'Blue is scattered all over the sky.'

Sound travels fastest in solids like steel, slower in liquids, slower still in gases, and not at all in a vacuum.
Memory hook: Tightly packed particles pass the sound fastest.

questions.q: Optical fibres work on the principle of:
questions.solution:
Light inside an optical fibre keeps hitting the walls at angles above the critical angle and is totally internally reflected, so it travels long distances.
Memory hook: Fibre, diamond, mirage — the TIR trio.

questions.q: Passengers fall forward when a moving bus stops suddenly. This is explained by:
questions.solution:
The upper body tends to keep moving (inertia of motion) while the feet stop with the bus — Newton's first law.
Memory hook: First law = bodies 'want' to keep doing what they were doing.

questions.q: A light year is a unit of:
questions.solution:
A light year is the distance light travels in one year (about 9.46 × 1012 km).
Memory hook: 'Year' fools you — it is how far, not how long.

questions.q: An object is placed beyond 2F of a convex lens. The image formed is:
options: Between F and 2F, real, inverted, diminished
On the same side, virtual, erect, enlarged
questions.solution:
For an object beyond 2F, the convex lens forms a real, inverted and smaller image between F and 2F on the other side (used in cameras).
Memory hook: Far object → small image close to F (like a camera).

1 horsepower ≈ 746 watts.
Memory hook: 746 W is about three-quarters of a kilowatt.

flashcards.back: Red light is scattered least, so it is seen from far away
